title: PRD: Fidelity Chaos Experimentation and Rollback
author: Lena Ortiz
body:
Overview

This PRD describes the Fidelity Chaos Experimentation and Rollback (FCER) product: a controlled test harness and operational playbook to exercise fidelity degradation paths (quantization fallbacks, lower-tier model variants, prefix truncation, KV cache eviction) in production-like environments and verify automated rollback behavior before broad rollouts.

Motivation

Redwood’s adaptive-fidelity features reduce cost by degrading output fidelity in controlled ways. Customers must not observe uncontrolled regressions. We need a repeatable product that: (1) safely injects fidelity degradations across deployment modes, (2) validates observability signals and quality metrics, (3) exercises rollback/mitigation automations, and (4) provides summary artifacts for stakeholders and customer communication.

Goals (measurable)

1. Provide a repeatable experiment runner that can execute 10 common fidelity-degradation scenarios against a tenant-configured workload within 1 hour.
2. Surface fidelity regressions on the platform dashboard within 2 minutes of divergence from baseline metrics (latency, token quality, token rejection rate).
3. Validate automated rollback policies (canary abort, model variant fallback, credit-safe fallback) succeed 95% of the time in controlled experiments.
4. Produce an experiment report (JSON + human-readable summary) for every run with deterministic artifacts for audit and legal.

Non-goals

- We will not implement new model quantization kernels. This product tests and validates existing runtime behaviors.
- We will not automate customer-visible price changes as part of an experiment.

Stakeholders and Owners

- Product (owner): Lena Ortiz (owner)
- Eng - Serving Runtime: Marcus Chen (technical lead)
- Eng - Observability: Priya Rao (telemetry & alerting)
- SRE / Reliability: Diego Alvarez (runbook & escalation)
- Legal & Compliance: Arjun Mehta (audit requirements)
- Customer Success: Mei Wallace (customer communication)

User Personas

- Internal QA engineers: run experiments and review artifacts.
- Platform engineers: validate rollout policies in staging and canary.
- Customer success / account teams: review experiment summaries for opt-in customers.

Functional Requirements

1. Experiment Definition API (REST + CLI): users must be able to define experiments with fields: name, description, target_tenants (list), degradation_type (enum), start_window (UTC), duration_minutes, traffic_shape (example: 5% ramp to 25% p50), baseline_reference (snapshot id), rollback_policy (enum), monitoring_tags (list).

2. Supported Degradation Types (initial):
   - quantization-profile-switch (e.g., q8 -> q4)
   - model-variant-lower-tier (e.g., rlx-3 => rlx-3-small)
   - kv-cache-eviction (evict prefix caches for specified session ids)
   - prefix-truncation (truncate input prompts above N tokens)
   - batching-constraint (force smaller batch sizes to emulate latency pressure)

3. Safe Execution Guards:

   - Experiments may only run against tenants that opted-in; system must prevent cross-tenant bleed.
   - A kill switch must allow immediate abort across all affected nodes.
   - Concurrency cap: max 3 parallel experiments per region.

4. Telemetry and Quality Signals:

   - Capture token-level loss delta, generation perplexity delta, latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), token error rates, allocator OOM events, and downstream client error rates.
   - Emit a 1-minute aggregated metrics snapshot to the observability pipeline for the experiment window.

5. Automated Rollback Policies (must support):

   - Threshold-based rollback (if quality_loss > X% or latency increase > Yms for Z min).
   - Canary abort if canary cohort shows regression > threshold versus baseline.
   - Escalation policy: if automatic rollback fails, create a high-severity incident and notify SRE.

6. Reporting and Artifact Storage:

   - Each experiment must store: experiment.json (definition), metrics_diff.csv, sample_generation_diffs.jsonl (10k lines cap), and human_summary.md.
   - Retention default: 90 days; export to S3 for audits via manual export.

Non-functional Requirements

- Security: experiments run under tenant-scoped IAM; logs must redact PII.
- Performance: experiment orchestration must add <2% overhead to runtime latency outside the experiment window.
- Reliability: experiment runner SLA 99.9% for orchestration APIs.
- Compliance: audit trail (who launched, approvals, timestamps) must be immutable for 2 years for flagged customers.

Acceptance Criteria

- QA team successfully runs the provided starter suite (10 scenarios) in staging and can reproduce a rollback within 5 minutes when a threshold is met.
- Dashboard surfaces experiment status and key deltas as specified.
- Generated report includes example diffs and enough context for CS to craft customer comms.

UX and Operator Flows

1. Create experiment (UI + CLI):

   - UI shows: experiment name, target tenant(s), degradation type, ramp schedule editor (prebuilt templates), expected impact box (auto-calculated from baseline), approval workflow (optional).

2. Preflight checks (automated):

   - validate tenant opt-in, validate model compatibility matrix, validate rollback policy presence, validate monitoring hooks ready.

3. Run + Monitor:

   - Live dashboard: status, traffic shape, top 10 metric deltas, sample diffs (toggle redact), auto-suggested rollback triggers.

4. Post-run report and signoff:

   - Role-based signoff flow: QA signs off to promote policy to production. CS receives sanitized summary for customers.

Rollout Plan (phased)

- Phase 0 (Pilot - 6 weeks): internal-only in staging with synthetic workloads. Deliverables: API, CLI, baseline dashboard, report generator.
- Phase 1 (Canary - 8 weeks): limited beta with 5 engineering tenants and 2 opt-in customers; expose UI and automated rollback.
- Phase 2 (GA - 12 weeks): self-serve opt-in in Console, retention policies, export tools, documentation and runbooks.

Metrics and Success Criteria

- % of experiments that auto-rollback within policy window (target: >= 95%).
- Mean time from regression detection to rollback (target: <= 3 minutes).
- False-positive rollback rate in staging (target: < 2%).
- Customer-reported fidelity incidents post-rollout (target: none for opted-in customers; monitor and escalate).

Experiment Configuration Matrix (example table)

| Scenario ID | Degradation Type | Traffic Shape | Rollback Trigger | Expected Impact | Owner |
|-------------|------------------|---------------|------------------|-----------------|-------|
| S-QUANT-1   | quantization-profile-switch | 10% -> 50% over 10m | quality_loss > 4% p95 | small drop in BLEU-like metric | QA Team |
| S-VARIANT-2 | model-variant-lower-tier | steady 5% | latency p95 + 40ms | higher hallucination risk | Serving Runtime |
| S-KV-3      | kv-cache-eviction | burst 20% 2m | client_error_rate > 0.5% | transient latency spike | SRE |

Operational Runbook (summary)

1. Abort: click Abort on experiment console -> orchestration sends kill to agents -> system verifies rollback completion across nodes.
2. If rollback fails: open /incident/new with template: "FCER rollback failed: <experiment-id>", tag SRE and Observability.
3. Post-incident: capture sample diffs and attach to incident for analysis.

Security, Privacy, and Compliance Notes

- All sample outputs must be sanitized and PII redacted before persistent storage. The experiment API must log the identity of the person who started the test and any approvers.
- For regulated customers, experiments are only allowed with explicit contract addendum; enforce at API level.

Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: noisy telemetry leads to false rollbacks. Mitigation: require sustained threshold for Z minutes, apply statistical smoothing, and provide simulation mode.
- Risk: cross-tenant exposure. Mitigation: strict tenant scoping, synthetic traffic isolation, and preflight checks.

Appendix: Example CLI snippets

# redacted example
cat exp.json | redwood experiments create --region us-west-2 --token $TOKEN

  "name": "quant-test-qa-2026-07",
  "target_tenants": ["tenant-acme-inc"],

  "duration_minutes": 30,
  "traffic_shape": "ramp: 5->25 over 10m",
  "rollback_policy": "threshold:quality_loss>3%:sustained:3m"
}

Acceptance signoff checklist

- [ ] API implemented and tested in staging
- [ ] UI experiment builder exists with templates
- [ ] Telemetry hook integrated with observability pipeline
- [ ] Rollback policies execute in 95% of test runs
- [ ] Documentation and runbook published

Open questions

1. What default thresholds should we ship for quality_loss vs latency to minimize customer impact? (Product & Serving Runtime to propose).
2. Should experiment exports be automatically pushed to customer-owned S3 for regulated customers?
